direction: C (round 3, rmf_survey): is the J0614-3329 radius (10.29 +1.01/-0.86 km at 1.44 Msun) versus nuclear-shell-structure tension generic for published relativistic mean-field models?

declared_before_compute.content: 18 parameter sets (3 session models re-run as regression + 11 requested + 4 extra published sets), 1 percent validation rule, the joint verdict copied from COMMON.md, ground-state check definition, derived quantities (m*/M, K, J, L, s_V, DD flag), the correlation plan and the optional diagnostic map grid; hash re-verified by every run script

key_results: (1) No published RMF model passes the joint verdict: 0 of 17 validated sets converge (DD-MEX dropped at validation). Every one fails J0614: |z_PIT| = 2.14 (TW99) to 5.03 (NL-SH); R_eq(1.44) = 12.48-15.39 km against the |z| < 2 bound 12.34 km. 15/17 pass 16O (only NL-rho 2.74 and GM1 3.88 MeV fail), 17/17 pass the ground-state check, 0/17 pass the 2-sigma box.

Best published model TW99 (DD, m*/M 0.555, L 55.3): chi2 = 11.15, p(nu=8) = 0.193, z J0614 = -2.14 is its only |z| >= 2; 16O 6.99 MeV; it is squeezed between J0614 (R_eq(1.44) = 12.48 km) and the J0740 radius (R(2.07) = 10.93 km, z = +1.87, M_max = 2.076 just above 2.07). Box: fails only R144.

Sensitivity without J0614 (7 terms, nu = 7): 5 published models converge (S7 and O and G): TW99 (p 0.489, max|z| 1.87), FSUGarnet (0.277, 1.63), DD-ME1 (0.243, 1.98), DD2 (0.230, 1.99), FSU2R (0.205, 1.65); DD-ME2 just misses (max|z| 2.02, R1418). With static radii (declared secondary configuration) TW99 passes S (chi2 10.60, p 0.225, max|z| 1.97): its verdict is decided by the 0.165 km Hartle-Thorne correction.

(2) The 16O splitting is a function of m*/M alone: split = 19.83 - 22.62 m*/M MeV across the 17 models (r = -0.96, R^2 = 0.93; equivalently V-S at n0, r = 0.96); independent of L (r = -0.19). In the map split = 18.58 - 22.17 m*/M + 1.09 s_V (R^2 = 0.991); the 4.9 MeV edge sits at m*/M = 0.645-0.657 for every zeta and L.

R_eq(1.44) across the published models is controlled by L (r = 0.83) and the high-density vector softening s_V = V(3n0)/(3V(n0)) (r = 0.61); P_beta(2n0) r = 0.82; raw m*/M r = 0.12 (published m*/M are clustered at 0.555-0.634 by shell structure), DD flag r = -0.30. OLS R_eq = 13.50 - 7.22 m*/M + 0.0244 L + 3.43 s_V (R^2 = 0.92, rms 0.24 km); partial correlations m*/M -0.77, L +0.93, s_V +0.84. In the map (fixed saturation): R_eq = 15.82 - 10.53 m*/M + 0.0138 L + 3.79 s_V (R^2 = 0.96, rms 0.14 km). M_max correlates with P_beta(3n0) (r = 0.97) and s_V (0.78).

The trade-off: at fixed m*/M (fixed by 16O) R(1.44) is lowered only by lower L and by vector softening, and softening costs M_max. Exchange rate dR_eq(1.44)/dM_max: 1.34-1.46 km per Msun for omega^4 (zeta 0 -> 0.06 in the map), 2.5-2.9 km per Msun for density-dependent couplings (DD-ME2/DD2/DD-ME1 -> TW99). DD couplings soften at 2-3 n0 and then saturate (f_omega(inf) = 0.70 for TW99; s_V(7n0) = 0.54, against 0.40 for FSUGold at the same s_V(2n0) = 0.77 and 0.48 for IUFSU/FSU2R/FSUGarnet with s_V(2n0) = 0.84), so they keep more M_max per km of radius.

Allowed region (J0614 |z| < 2 AND 16O in window AND M_max >= 1.94): EMPTY among the 17 published models and among the 65 map points. Any two of the three can be met: J0614 + 16O only with zeta >= 0.045, L = 40, m*/M 0.60-0.64 (M_max 1.69-1.78); J0614 + M_max only at m*/M >= 0.75, L = 40, zeta = 0 (16O 2.72 MeV, M_max 2.06); 16O + M_max only with R_eq(1.44) >= 12.87 km (map) / 12.48 km (TW99, published). The (m*/M, L, M_max) window both J0614 and shell structure allow is m*/M <= 0.65, L ~ 40, M_max <= 1.79 Msun, excluded by J0740 (mass z >= 4.2).

(3) NVG: stable members have m*/M >= 0.83 (posterior 0.853), V-S(n0) = 77-259 MeV vs 406-759 MeV for the RMF sets; their 16O splittings 0.23-1.48 MeV lie on the continuation of the RMF split(m*/M) curve (map: 2.71 MeV at 0.76, 2.05 at 0.80; NVG 1.45-1.48 at 0.83-0.84, 1.04 at 0.87, 0.67 at 0.90). The density shape of V-S is RMF-like ((V-S)(n0/2)/(V-S)(n0) = 0.50-0.62 vs 0.52-0.62), so the shell-structure failure of NVG is the same m*/M physics as in RMF.

NVG sits on the J0614 side of the divide (high m*/M) but does not collect the RMF radius advantage there: R_eq(1.44) posterior median 12.61 km (M_max 1.956, L 56.4) vs 11.87-12.28 km at M_max 1.88-1.90 for an RMF with m*/M = 0.80, zeta = 0, L = 40-70. Reason: its vector self-energy V = C_v n / y^2 STIFFENS with density (s_V(3n0) = 1.12-1.34 for the named members; every RMF set has s_V <= 1), because the vector mass q W tracks the falling scalar. NVG therefore misses both: shell structure by ~0.19 in m*/M, J0614 at |z_LOO| = 2.39.

verdict_text: The tension is generic for relativistic mean-field models. Of 17 validated published parametrizations (NL3, NL-SH, NL3wrho, TM1, GM1, NL-rho, FSUGold, FSU2, FSU2R, FSU2H, FSUGarnet, IUFSU, BigApple, DD-ME1, DD-ME2, DD2, TW99; DD-MEX dropped at validation) none converges under the declared joint verdict: all 17 fail the J0614 radius (|z| 2.14-5.03), while 15 pass the 16O splitting and all pass the ground-state check. The splitting fixes m*/M <= 0.65; at that Dirac mass R(1.44) can be pulled below 12.34 km only by vector softening, which drops M_max below the J0740 mass (map: M_max <= 1.79 where J0614 and 16O both pass). Any two of {J0614, 16O, M_max >= 1.94} are compatible, all three are not, in the published set and in the 65-point FSU-type map. Density-dependent couplings get closest (TW99: one term at z = -2.14, p = 0.19; passes with static radii; five models converge when J0614 is left out). NVG sits on the other side of the same divide: m*/M >= 0.83 kills the splitting for the same Dirac reason, and its density-stiffening vector keeps R(1.44) at 12.6 km.
practical_value: A ready per-model table (joint_verdict_table) of 17 validated published RMF sets through one pipeline (SLy crust, consistent pressure, Hartle-Thorne equatorial radii at the NICER spins): chi2 and each term's z for the 8-datum likelihood, 2-sigma box, the 16O/40Ca/208Pb LDA splittings, M_max, R_eq(1.44), Lambda_tilde, P_beta(2n0).

Rule of thumb for RMF builders: 16O 1p splitting (LDA) ~ 19.8 - 22.6 m*/M MeV, so shell structure needs m*/M <= 0.65; then R_eq(1.44) ~ 13.5 - 7.2 m*/M + 0.024 L + 3.4 s_V km (published sets, rms 0.24 km). J0614 at 2 sigma needs R_eq(1.44) < 12.34 km (static ~12.15 km after the ~0.17-0.21 km rotation correction).

Vector softening by density-dependent couplings buys about twice as much radius reduction per unit M_max as an omega^4 term (2.5-2.9 vs 1.3-1.5 km per Msun); a model that softens at 2-3 n0 and stiffens back at 5-7 n0 is the only RMF direction toward J0614 + J0740 + 16O. TW99 is the published set closest to all data.
If J0614 is set aside, TW99, FSUGarnet, FSU2R, DD-ME1 and DD2 pass the same declared joint test (p 0.20-0.49); J0614 alone separates 'all fail' from 'five pass'.
The rotation correction matters: for TW99 the 0.165 km Hartle-Thorne shift of R(1.44) flips the J0614 verdict (z -1.97 static vs -2.14 rotating).
caveats: Parameters are recalled from the papers; the 1 percent saturation check validates 17 sets (worst deviations 0.0-0.82 percent) and rejected DD-MEX (L off by 6.5 percent). A compensating error that leaves all six saturation properties within 1 percent cannot be excluded.

IUFSU's m*/M and NL3wrho's isoscalar properties were not validated separately (see validation.not_validated_properties); NL3wrho uses the recalled Lambda_v = 0.03 with g_rho from the Horowitz-Piekarewicz prescription.

The 16O splitting is the session's LDA procedure (fixed Fermi profile, U_SEP, Woods-Saxon fit, first-order l.s), validated on NL3/DD-ME2/FSUGold against 6.18 MeV; it is not a self-consistent finite-nucleus RMF calculation. The m*/M <= 0.65 bound is the procedure's, though the standard self-consistent lore gives the same range.

The fixed-model criterion uses z_PIT; TW99 fails by 0.14 in z (0.14 km). The all-|z|<2 rule rejects a correct model about 30 percent of the time (creative/likelihood/refute.json), so TW99's failure is weak evidence on its own; the generic statement rests on all 17 failing J0614 and on the empty three-way region of the map.

The map is one FSU-type family at one saturation point (n0 0.152, E/A -16.2, K 240, S_2(0.10) 25.5) on a 7 x 5 x 2 grid; a DD-type map was not built, so the statement 'all three cannot be met' is shown for NL-type models and for the published DD sets, not for every DD functional. Extrapolating the DD exchange rate from TW99 would need M_max ~2.02 for R_eq = 12.34 km, but the J0740 radius term (z +1.87 already) would then fail; this is an extrapolation, not computed.
All models are purely nucleonic (no hyperons, quarks); SLy crust for all (FSU2R matches at 0.71 n0); M_max is static (rotation adds ~0.01 Msun).
NVG numbers are taken from earlier session results (creative/likelihood, creative/spin_orbit); only the V(n), S(n) profiles of four named members were computed here.
